Use `waterfall-direct-api` when you want an agent to retrieve data for a task now: a contact lookup, a company lookup, a verification check, or a small evaluation. The skill guides HTTP requests, authentication, result handling, pagination, and errors. For a maintained workflow in your application, use [Build an integration](/v1/skills-integration).

## Install the skill

```
npx skills add Waterfall-io/api-skills --skill waterfall-direct-api
```

The skill is published in the [Waterfall API Skills repository](https://github.com/Waterfall-io/api-skills). API calls require an authorized Waterfall key; installing the skill does not provide access. Store the key in the execution environment, as described in [Authentication](/v1/authentication).

## Example task

> I have three LinkedIn profile URLs. Use Waterfall to return each person’s available name, job title, and company name, with the original URL beside each result. Choose the endpoint from the current docs. I do not need emails or phone numbers. Show the requests before making live calls, and leave unavailable fields empty.

This task gives the agent a known input, specific output fields, and a record limit. [Choose an API](/v1/introduction) explains which endpoint fits. See [use cases](/v1/use-cases/overview) for other starting points.

## Review the result

Check that the result answers your task and that missing matches or fields remain visible. A completed API job does not guarantee a complete profile. Use the returned job ID to retrieve asynchronous results rather than launching the lookup again. Read [Usage Tracking](/v1/inline-usage) for costs when they are available in the result. Calls use your account’s configured rates. Use the current endpoint reference if it differs from the skill’s instructions. For code that your team will maintain, continue to [Build an integration](/v1/skills-integration).
